block_suggestions.outcome: Independently locate an input check, explain branch conditions and choose a debugger observation that can falsify your guess.
block_suggestions.diagnostic: In 10 minutes, inspect gdb_disassembly only: mark the two conditional branches, identify the strcmp call, and state why testing EAX after it selects success/failure. If correct, skip both intro videos and begin the exercise.

Attempt branch reconstruction and output table without source

block_suggestions.preparation: Save both raw companion files separately; keep source hidden until assessment. A paper exercise requires only saved files. Optional lab requires a locally compiled or otherwise vetted benign program, working Ghidra/GDB and dependencies checked before departure.
block_suggestions.exercise: From published disassembly, draw branches at main+19 and main+76. Predict output classes for no argument, one wrong argument, one correct argument, and two arguments. Explain which operation reveals the unknown correct string; do not pretend the disassembly listing contains its bytes. Choose an observation immediately after strcmp that distinguishes a correct input from a bypassed branch.
block_suggestions.assessment: argc must equal 2 (program name counts); otherwise Usage. With exactly one argument, the program prints Checking License and then WRONG or Access Granted according to strcmp==0. The provided source supplies the exact key. test eax,eax followed by jne selects WRONG when EAX is nonzero. Setting a register to force success is a bypass, not proof you recovered the key. For an optional live lab, record input, strcmp return and observed branch; do not reuse published addresses after recompilation.
block_suggestions.offline_fallback: Paper-only: annotate the supplied disassembly and compare all four output cases against license_1.c. This assesses control-flow reasoning, not demonstrated GUI/debugger operation.
block_suggestions.execution_status: Source/disassembly inspected; lab and learner exercise not executed.

block_suggestions.outcome: Choose capability matching, string recovery or signature scanning appropriately, and route .NET/Android/Python files to the right approved family.
block_suggestions.diagnostic: In five minutes explain: why a capability match is not proof of execution; why strings can miss text; why extracting a PyInstaller archive does not imply decompiled Python.
block_suggestions.preparation: Save selected Markdown/YARA sections. Optional rule execution needs working YARA checked beforehand; paper truth-table work needs no lab or sample malware.
block_suggestions.exercise: Write a YARA rule with $a="alpha" nocase and $b="token" and condition $a and $b. Predict matches for four ASCII text files: A="ALPHA token", B="alpha TOKEN", C="token alone", D="alphabet token". Then explain why the default capa output can hide a nested set-registry-value match under persistence, and which verbosity flags expose more evidence.
block_suggestions.assessment: A and D match; B fails because token remains case sensitive, and C lacks alpha. D exposes a substring false positive: explain whether adding fullword to alpha would fit the intended question. Optional CLI: save four .txt files plus rule.yar, run yara rule.yar A.txt (repeat each file), and compare emitted rule names with the table. capa -v exposes nested matches, -vv explains matching evidence; a match is not proof the action actually ran.
block_suggestions.offline_fallback: Compute the rule truth table from saved YARA docs and answer the capa nested-match question from the pinned guide. No malware, portal, network or tool execution is required.
block_suggestions.execution_status: Documentation inspected and expected answers derived; YARA not executed.

family_rationales.rationale: dnSpyEx is the sole selected managed-code routing reference. Native Ghidra/GDB proficiency does not establish .NET expertise; keep a short reference until a real managed assembly warrants a separate lab.

JADX orientation covers APK/DEX and manifest/resource navigation. Apktool, dex2jar, Android Studio, Bytecode Viewer and Fernflower retain exact approved-row references; separate overlapping introductions would crowd out practice. APK modification/emulation and native JNI need a separate prepared lab.

pyinstxtractor-ng is a short extraction reference; pycdc/uncompyle6/unpyc3 remain bytecode-version-specific references, not interchangeable guarantees. Read supported input versions rather than inferring support from the host Python runtime.
Ghidra and stock GDB provide the core workflow. x64dbg/OllyDbg/Cutter/radare2 and GEF/peda/pwndbg remain approved reference choices; no need to relearn the same branch task in every interface.

capa/FLOSS/YARA establish static triage roles. Existing approved references for Didier tools, oletools, FakeNet-NG, AutoIt and format-specific unpackers remain available; no live-malware plane lab is required or proposed.

angr/ROPgadget remain references for a challenge that actually needs path constraints or gadgets. General native input-check recovery is a prerequisite; adding advanced courses without a diagnostic gap would dilute this refresher.
